messages.content: Can you give current weather conditions in Hyderabad?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve data such as web pages or API responses. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. Must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL.

headers.description: A dictionary containing HTTP headers to send with the request.

timeout.description: The maximum number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. A single value specifies a general timeout. A tuple specifies a connect timeout and read timeout respectively, in seconds. This is a float type value.

location.description: The location parameter specifies the desired location for weather information, such as 'Berkeley, CA' or 'New York, NY'.

params.description: Query parameters to be sent in the URL of the GET request. For example, specifying a location to get weather information.

auth.description: A tuple representing HTTP authentication credentials in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem) or a tuple of (certificate file, key file) as file system paths.

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to attach to the request.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be immediately downloaded.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not.

message.reasoning:
We need to fetch current weather conditions in Hyderabad. We can use the requests_get tool. We'll call it with url "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast" maybe. But we need to know what API to use. The tool description says "Query parameters to be sent in the URL of the GET request. For example, specifying a location to get weather information." It includes location param. So likely we should use open-meteo API. Let's check typical usage: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=...&longitude=...&current_weather=true. But the tool expects location param? Actually the params dict has location optional string. That might be used by some other API like openweathermap. But open-meteo uses lat/lon. However the tool's description may be generic. We could use open-meteo with lat/lon for Hyderabad: latitude 17.3850, longitude 78.4867. Provide current_weather=true.

Let's call requests_get with url "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast" and params {latitude: 17.3850, longitude: 78.4867, current_weather:true}. But the params type expects keys location, format etc. Not latitude. But maybe it's flexible. The tool signature shows params: {location?: string, format?: ...}. But we can pass additional keys? Might cause error. Alternatively we can use openweathermap API: http://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather?q=Hyderabad&appid=API_KEY. But we don't have an API key. Could use wttr.in? e.g., https://wttr.in/Hyderabad?format=j1. That returns JSON. No auth needed. So we can use that. Use url "https://wttr.in/Hyderabad?format=j1". No params needed. Then parse JSON.

Thus call requests_get with url "https://wttr.in/Hyderabad?format=j1". No headers. Then parse result. Let's do that.
